newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary says no more maize export licences for now.
newsitem.headline: Hungary says no more maize export licences for now.

text.p: Hungary does not plan to issue further maize export licences, as excess stocks roughly match the amount already allowed to be exported, officials said on Thursday.
"The export base and the issued licences are in parity," Bela Kovacs, head of department at the Agricultural Regulatory Office, told Reuters.
He also confirmed that the latest batch of export licences for 200,000 tonnes of maize had been exhausted.
Industry sources are divided on the exact size of Hungary's excess maize stock but Kovacs said he estimated it to be between 600,000 and 700,000 tonnes.
He added that the office does not know to what extent existing export licences have been used as they can only rely on quarterly customs statistics.
Hungary harvested 6.2 million tonnes of maize in 1996 from 1.1 million hectares.
FOT (free on truck) maize prices in Hungary are between 17,600 and 18,300 forints per tonne.
The country's agricultural and food foreign trade balance showed an $2.2 billion surplus last year, while the overall foreign trade balance showed a deficit of $2.65 billion.
Most of landlocked Hungary's grains exports go to neighbouring countries.
